title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
content: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
content: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
content: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

title: The Real Competitiveness Test
content: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

title: Our AI, Your Problem
content: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
content: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
content: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
content: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

title: The Twilight of the ICC
content: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
content: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
content: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

title: The Return of the Power Trust
content: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
content: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
content: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

title: The Rise of the Token Economy
content: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
content: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
content: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
content: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
content: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
content: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

title: The Last Trump Election
content: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
content: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
content: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.
